newsitem.title: GERMANY: Viag sees 1996 profits at least equal to 95.
newsitem.headline: Viag sees 1996 profits at least equal to 95.

text.p: Munich-based diversified industrial group Viag AG said it expected 1996 pre-tax profits to be at least equal to those in 1995, while group turnover should rise to some 45 billion marks ($28.9 billion).
"The pre-tax profit will be at least equal to that in 1995 and even a little better," Viag chief executive Georg Obermeier told journalists late on Wednesday evening.
In 1995, Viag made a pre-tax profit of 2.2 billion marks on turnover of 41.9 billion.
Obermeier said that in 1997 Viag could expect turnover and profits "a bit better" than in 1996.

However he added that Viag's orginal plan to have its energy division account for just 50 percent of profits, with its other activities taking up the other half, would not be realised in the mid-term.
Energy would continue to contribute at least 60 percent to profits in five years time, he estimated.
